extracted.intended_audience: professional journalists, editors, newsroom staff, journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: A concise ethical framework for professional journalism describing principles reporters and editors should follow when gathering, reporting, and correcting news. Emphasizes truth-telling, minimizing harm, independence, accountability, and themes relevant to newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It
rubrics_metrics.description: "Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when unpopular; give voice to the voiceless — official and unofficial sources can be equally valid; recognize a special obligation to ensure public business is conducted in the open and government records open to inspection; examine your own cultural values and avoid imposing them on others; avoid stereotyping; report differences explicitly; consider the long-term implications of decisions; distinguish news from advertising and entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ethical journalists treat sources, subjects and colleagues as human beings deserving of respect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the public's right to know against potential harm; show compassion for those affected by news coverage; be sensitive when seeking or using interviews/photos of those affected by tragedy; recognize that legal access to information differs from ethical justification to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently
rubrics_metrics.description: "Journalists should be free of obligation to any interest other than the public's right to know."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived; refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel, special treatment; distinguish news from sponsored content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable and Transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: "Journalists are accountable to their readers, listeners, viewers and each other."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences; encourage civil dialogue with the public; acknowledge and correct mistakes promptly and prominently; expose unethical conduct in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public's Right to Know
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundational criterion for what to publish: prioritize information the public needs to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the public's right to know as a primary justification for reporting while weighing it against potential harm; prioritize coverage that reveals matters of public interest or accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Business / Government Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: A special obligation to ensure public business is conducted in the open and government records open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue transparency in government affairs; investigate and report on public institutions and officials to hold them accountable; prioritize access to and reporting on public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of Human Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report across different communities and perspectives; examine and avoid imposing one's own cultural values; avoid stereotyping and report differences explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give Voice to the Voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide coverage and sources for individuals and groups who lack power or access in public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat official and unofficial sources as potentially valid; seek out underrepresented perspectives and include them responsibly in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Long-term Consequences vs. Short-term Clicks
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh the long-term implications of editorial decisions rather than prioritizing immediate attention or clicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism that sacrifices public trust; consider downstream effects of publication on individuals and communities when deciding what and how to publish.
